message.content: No. A generated output that is substantially similar to a training item does not prove memorization. The similarity might arise from generalization. For instance, if 100 training examples share a common structure, a model may produce text resembling a specific training item simply by applying 5 learned general patterns. A correlation of 0.8 between training and generated outputs does not uniquely identify memorization. Even among 100 examples, a 0.9 similarity score may simply reflect learned rules.
